newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori's lawyer says president born in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori's lawyer says president born in Peru.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori's family lawyer said on Friday the head of state was born in Peru, countering media reports that claimed he may be ineligible to rule because he was born in Japan.

With the Peruvian constitution requiring presidents to be born in Peru, lawyer Sandro Fuentes told a news conference in Government Palace that Fujimori's birth certificate proved he was born in the capital, Lima.
"I have the professional conviction that Mr. Alberto Fujimori is Peruvian by birth," Fuentes said, distributing copies of the president's birth certificate to journalists.

Fujimori, the 58-year-old son of Japanese immigrants, also authorised an investigation examining documents that local opposition media claimed had been altered to change the name of the president's birthplace, Fuentes said.

The publication on Thursday of the documents by weekly magazine Caretas deepened a political crisis for Fujimori, who has plummeted in the polls to record lows following a slew of scandals involving the country's security forces.

But amid fears the latest attack on Fujimori cou lead the military to seize power, members of the opposition welcomed the measured response of the president, who has not personally commented on the media allegations.
"It is intelligent of the president to make the documents available to everybody that wants them so that this matter can be cleared up," said opposition congressman Freddy Ghilardi.
Most Peruvians have become increasingly hostile to Fujimori's perceived authoritarian style during his seven years in office.

But they also believe the head of Peru's intelligence service, Vladimiro Montesinos, and the country's armed forces chief Gen. Nicolas Bari de Hermoza wield more power than the president, according to local pollsters.
Observers have claimed Montesinos knew the president was born in Japan and used the information to blackmail him into granting increased powers to the security forces.
